intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges. Spot howler monkeys, toucans, and resplendent quetzals while gliding above the treetops at speeds up to 50 mph.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through jungle canals in a small boat guided by a certified naturalist to observe manatees, caimans, river otters, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the black-sand beaches at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a professional naturalist guide who uses high-powered telescopes to reveal sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, squirrel monkeys, and scarlet macaws hidden in the lush rainforest. The hike concludes at pristine white-sand beaches perfect for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Night Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided nocturnal hike around the base of the iconic Arenal Volcano to discover Costa Rica's hidden nightlife — red-eyed tree frogs, tarantulas, kinkajous, and sleeping birds. Expert guides illuminate the dark jungle trails and share fascinating insights into the rainforest ecosystem after dark.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition
experiences.description: Venture deep into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through old-growth primary rainforest with a licensed guide to encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, harpy eagles, and all four of Costa Rica's monkey species in their untouched natural habitat.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport soda (local diner) or a convenience snack before heading to the resort — budget around $5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle service like Interbus or Caribe Shuttle in advance to save money vs. private taxi. Keep $10–15 USD cash handy for tips and incidentals. Exchange some currency at the airport or use an ATM for colones.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a late breakfast, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get oriented. Watch for coastal wildlife such as pelicans, frigate birds, and hermit crabs along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town on foot or by bicycle rental ($5–8/day). Visit the local mercado (market) to pick up fresh tropical fruits like mangoes, papayas, and pineapples for cheap snacking throughout the trip. Stroll through the town center and get familiar with local sodas and budget eateries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset on the beach. Head to a nearby local soda for a traditional casado dinner (rice, beans, salad, protein) and a fresh fruit batido (smoothie).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast if included, or visit a local bakery/panadería for bread, coffee, and fruit — $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from the market and snacks — $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Casado at a local soda — $6–9 USD including drink

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally low-key to recover from travel. Use this day to download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline), buy a local SIM card (Kölbi or Claro, ~$10 with data), and plan logistics for the rest of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along a nearby nature trail or beach at sunrise (5:30–6:00 AM). February is dry season, making it ideal for wildlife spotting. Look for howler monkeys, iguanas, and tropical birds. Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget-friendly group zip-lining tour in the nearby area. Many operators offer packages starting at $35–55 USD for 8–12 platforms. Book through the hotel or a local operator to avoid tourist markup. Zip-lining through the rainforest canopy is a must-do eco-adventure experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local open-air restaurant for fresh grilled fish or chicken with rice and beans. Enjoy the warm evening air and share stories with fellow travelers at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans with egg) at a local soda — $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch of fruit and granola bars before zip-lining, or eat at the zip-line operator's on-site café — $5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish at a local open-air restaurant — $8–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining at least 1 day in advance. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable clothes. Apply sunscreen and insect repellent. Bring a small daypack with water (at least 1.5L), snacks, and a light rain jacket even in dry season.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget public bus or shared shuttle to a nearby national park or wildlife refuge (options vary by resort location — e.g., Manuel Antonio, Tortuguero, or Corcovado area). Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) when wildlife is most active. Look for sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, coatis, and toucans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park trails. Many parks have self-guided trails — purchase a park entrance ticket ($18–20 USD for most Costa Rican national parks). Swim at a park beach if available and permitted. Avoid peak midday heat by resting in shaded areas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by shared shuttle or public bus. Grab dinner at a local soda and reflect on the day's wildlife sightings. Write down or photograph your wildlife checklist.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — gallo pinto and coffee at resort or local soda — $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the market (sandwiches, fruit, crackers) — $4–6 USD. No outside food allowed in some parks; check rules in advance.
meals.dinner: Soda dinner — casado or arroz con pollo — $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Hire a local naturalist guide at the park entrance for 2–3 hours ($20–30 USD split among a group of 2–4) — they dramatically improve wildlife spotting success. Bring a waterproof bag for cameras. Stay on marked trails at all times.

day_by_day.morning: Morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) rental along the coast or a nearby river estuary. Rentals typically cost $10–20 USD for 2 hours. Paddle through mangroves and watch for crocodiles, herons, and river otters in calmer waterways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or frog sanctuary if available in the area (entrance $10–15 USD). These small eco-attractions offer incredible close-up encounters with poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, and other exotic species. Great for wildlife photography.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event in town if available (check local boards). Otherwise, enjoy a beachfront walk at dusk and watch for bioluminescence in the water if conditions allow. Dinner at a local restaurant with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate and coffee at a local café — $4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Ceviche and patacones (fried plantains) at a beach shack — $6–8 USD
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken or fish with rice and salad at a local restaurant — $8–11 USD

day_by_day.notes: February evenings can be warm and breezy — perfect for outdoor dining. Check with locals about bioluminescent plankton conditions; some bays in Costa Rica are known for this phenomenon. Bring a headlamp for evening beach walks.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group white-water rafting tour on a nearby river (e.g., Río Savegre, Río Pacuare, or local equivalent depending on resort location). Half-day rafting trips start at $40–65 USD per person with group discounts. Class II–IV rapids offer thrills for all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, relax at the river base camp. Many operators include a simple lunch. Dry off, change clothes, and take a slow journey back to the resort. Stop at a roadside fruit stand for fresh coconut water ($1–2 USD) — a perfect post-adventure refreshment.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening at the resort. Socialize with other travelers, play cards, or use the resort's common areas. Try cooking a simple meal if kitchen facilities are available, using ingredients from the local market to save money.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before rafting — gallo pinto and juice — $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Often included with rafting tour, or roadside snacks — $0–5 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal using local ingredients (pasta, veggies, eggs) or soda dinner — $4–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book rafting through a certified operator with safety equipment included. Wear a swimsuit under quick-dry clothes. Secure all valuables in waterproof dry bags provided by the operator. This is one of the best value adventure activities in Costa Rica.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend the morning on the beach. Practice snorkeling if gear is available for rent ($5–10 USD) — February's dry season typically means calmer, clearer waters for coastal snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Sunday market or artisan fair if available. Pick up handmade souvenirs like carved wood items, hammocks, or local coffee at much cheaper prices than tourist shops. Budget $10–20 USD for souvenirs if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga on the beach (many resorts or local instructors offer free or donation-based sessions). Enjoy a special budget splurge dinner — try a slightly nicer local restaurant for fresh seafood or traditional Costa Rican cuisine without breaking the bank.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort or a nearby café with fresh juice and pancakes — $5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Market snacks and fresh fruit — $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated local seafood restaurant — $12–16 USD as a weekly treat

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a mental reset day. Use the afternoon to plan the second half of the trip, confirm any remaining bookings, and check your budget. Costa Rica's pura vida lifestyle is best embraced on slow days like this.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching tour or self-guided walk in a nearby cloud forest reserve or secondary forest area. February is excellent for birding — look for scarlet macaws, toucans, motmots, and tanagers. Bring binoculars and a field guide app like eBird or Merlin.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cacao or coffee farm for a budget tour ($10–20 USD). Learn about the farm-to-cup process, taste fresh cacao, and understand Costa Rica's agricultural heritage. Many farms offer chocolate-making demonstrations included in the tour price.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Join other travelers for a communal dinner or potluck if the resort facilitates it. Share travel tips and experiences. Otherwise, enjoy a quiet dinner at a local soda.

meals.breakfast: Pre-birding early breakfast — granola, yogurt, and coffee — $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Farm tour often includes light snacks; supplement with market fruit — $3–6 USD
meals.dinner: Soda dinner — olla de carne (beef stew) or sopa negra (black bean soup) — $6–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Download the Merlin Bird ID app by Cornell Lab before the trip — it's free and invaluable for identifying birds by sound and sight in Costa Rica. Birdwatching is best from 5:30–9:00 AM when birds are most active and temperatures are coolest.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby waterfall. Many stunning waterfalls in Costa Rica are accessible via short hikes (30–90 minutes each way) with little or no entrance fee. Swim in the natural pool at the base for a refreshing eco-adventure experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue waterfall exploration or hike a secondary trail in the same area. Look for wildlife along the trail — monkeys, sloths, and colorful frogs are commonly spotted in forested waterfall areas. Pack out all trash and follow Leave No Trace principles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort tired but exhilarated. Rinse off, rest, and head out for a casual dinner. Try a local pulpería (corner store) for cheap snacks and cold drinks if budget is tight.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast before the hike — rice and beans, egg, and coffee — $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch: peanut butter sandwiches, bananas, trail mix — $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda or pulpería snacks — $5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Waterfall trails can be slippery — wear hiking sandals or trail shoes with grip. Bring at least 2L of water per person. Start early to avoid afternoon heat and to have the waterfall to yourself before tour groups arrive. Check local conditions before hiking.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wildlife boat tour through a local river, estuary, or coastal mangrove system. Group tours start at $25–40 USD and offer sightings of crocodiles, caimans, Jesus Christ lizards, kingfishers, and various waterbirds. One of the best wildlife value experiences in Costa Rica.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the beach or resort pool after the morning tour. Alternatively, rent a bicycle ($5–8 USD) and explore coastal roads and nearby villages at your own pace. Stop at a local roadside stand for fresh pipa fría (cold green coconut).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural performance or live music event if available in town. Costa Rican towns often have free community events on weeknights. Otherwise, enjoy a beachside bonfire if permitted or a quiet evening stargazing (February skies are clear in dry season).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before boat tour — gallo pinto and café chino — $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Beachside ceviche or empanadas from a street vendor — $4–7 USD
meals.dinner: Grilled fish tacos at a local taco stand or soda — $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat tour the evening before through the resort or a local operator. Morning tours (6:00–8:00 AM departure) offer the best wildlife activity. Bring a camera with a zoom lens or use a smartphone with a clip-on telephoto lens for wildlife photography.

day_by_day.morning: Second zip-lining experience at a different operator or location if available, OR try a canopy walkway/hanging bridges tour through the rainforest ($20–35 USD). Hanging bridges offer a slower, more educational alternative to zip-lining with excellent wildlife viewing from the canopy level.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby wildlife rescue center or sanctuary ($10–20 USD entrance). These centers rehabilitate injured sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other animals. Ethical wildlife encounters without disturbing animals in the wild — a responsible eco-tourism choice.
day_by_day.evening: Final major adventure dinner — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate the trip's highlights. Try a local restaurant known for traditional Costa Rican cuisine like tamales, chifrijo, or a full seafood platter.

meals.breakfast: Café and toast with local jam at a bakery — $3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the rescue center café or packed snacks — $4–7 USD
meals.dinner: Traditional Costa Rican restaurant — $10–15 USD as a celebratory meal

day_by_day.notes: Research wildlife rescue centers in advance to ensure they follow ethical practices (no riding animals, no forced animal-tourist interactions). Reputable centers include Jaguar Rescue Center, Toucan Rescue Ranch, and Kids Saving the Rainforest, depending on your location.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach or nature trail — take photos, reflect on the trip, and soak in the pura vida atmosphere one last time. Look for any wildlife species you haven't spotted yet on your checklist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets or artisan shops. Buy Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, or handmade crafts as gifts. Pack bags and settle the hotel bill. Confirm departure transport arrangements for the next morning.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with fellow travelers or solo reflection meal at your favorite local soda discovered during the trip. Toast to an incredible eco-adventure with a glass of local guaro (sugarcane liquor) or a fresh fruit smoothie.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit bowl, yogurt, and granola at a café — $4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch — ceviche, patacones, or street food — $5–7 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at favorite local soda or restaurant — $8–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to reorganize your luggage, separate dirty clothes, and ensure all souvenirs are properly packed (no prohibited agricultural items like fresh fruit or soil). Double-check your passport, travel documents, and flight details for departure day.

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout from Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange shared shuttle or public bus to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO). Allow at least 3–4 hours before departure for travel time and airport check-in, especially if departing from a remote coastal area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport check-in, security, and departure procedures. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Costa Rican coffee or chocolate gifts (often comparable in price to local shops). Enjoy a final gallo pinto breakfast at an airport restaurant before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Board departure flight. Reflect on 13 days of eco-adventure, zip-lining, wildlife encounters, and pura vida living. Costa Rica will call you back!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto and coffee at airport soda or café — $6–9 USD (airport prices slightly higher)
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring snacks from the resort — $5–10 USD
meals.dinner: On the plane or at layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Budget travelers tip: Shared shuttles to the airport cost $20–35 USD vs. $80–120 USD for private taxis. Book 24–48 hours in advance. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Keep some colones for any last-minute airport expenses. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and accommodation): $400–600 USD for 13 days including activities, meals, and local transport.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack from the resort's late-night room service or a vending area upon arrival – keep it simple after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon late-night arrival. Have your resort confirmation and local currency (CRC) or USD ready. Do not schedule any activities for Day 1 – rest is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront to get your bearings, breathe the coastal air, and shake off jet lag. Explore the resort grounds and chat with the concierge about the week ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed guided resort nature walk or a short independent exploration of the immediate coastal area. Spot local birds, iguanas, and coastal wildlife. Visit a nearby local lookout point or beach cove for a gentle introduction to Costa Rica's natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the beachfront. Head to a nearby casual open-air restaurant for a traditional Costa Rican dinner featuring gallo pinto, fresh ceviche, and local beer or fruit juice.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort – casado plate with rice, beans, plantains, and grilled fish (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Mid-range open-air seafood restaurant near the beachfront – fresh catch of the day, patacones, and a local Imperial beer (~$20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Hydrate well, apply sunscreen, and purchase any missing supplies at a nearby farmacia or supermarket. Exchange currency if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the journey toward Manuel Antonio National Park (if the resort is in the Central Pacific region) or arrange a day-trip transfer. Arrive early at Manuel Antonio National Park for the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike. Your certified naturalist guide uses high-powered spotting scopes to find sloths, squirrel monkeys, white-faced capuchins, toucans, and poison dart frogs hidden in the lush jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided eco-hike, enjoy free time on the park's stunning white-sand beaches – Playa Manuel Antonio is one of Costa Rica's most beautiful. Swim, snorkel in the calm waters, or simply relax and watch the resident monkeys play nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy dinner at a recommended restaurant in the Manuel Antonio village strip, known for its vibrant dining scene with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – grab a packed breakfast or eat from the buffet by 7:00 AM
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or purchase from a vendor inside/near the park entrance – fresh fruit, sandwiches, and coconut water (~$5–10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante La Luna or similar mid-range restaurant in Manuel Antonio village – sea bass in garlic butter, tropical salad, and fresh lemonade (~$22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Manuel Antonio Guided Eco-Hike in advance as spots fill quickly. Wear lightweight, moisture-wicking clothing, sturdy walking shoes, and bring insect repellent. Park entry fee is approximately $20 USD per person. Arrive at the park by 7:00–8:00 AM for the best wildlife sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart early toward Arenal Volcano / La Fortuna area (approximately 3.5–4.5 hours by shuttle or private transfer depending on your resort's location). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's Central Valley and rolling hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in La Fortuna and check into a mid-range lodge with Arenal Volcano views. After settling in, visit the iconic La Fortuna Waterfall – a 70-meter cascade surrounded by rainforest. Hike down the 500+ steps to the base for a refreshing swim in the natural pool.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot springs near Arenal Volcano. Mid-range options like Baldi Hot Springs or Tabacon offer multiple thermal pools and a relaxing atmosphere perfect after a travel day.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before departure or stop at a roadside soda en route
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local soda in La Fortuna town – rice and bean casado with chicken or fish (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Don Rufino or similar mid-range restaurant in La Fortuna – Costa Rican beef tenderloin, yuca fries, and tropical juice (~$20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your shuttle transfer from the resort area to La Fortuna in advance. Shared shuttle services like Interbus or Gray Line are reliable and mid-range budget friendly (~$35–55 per person). La Fortuna Waterfall entrance fee is approximately $18 USD. Bring a swimsuit and water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Arenal Volcano Night Wildlife Walk – booked for this evening, so the morning is free. Start the day with a guided birdwatching walk around your lodge grounds. Arenal's surrounding forests are home to over 500 bird species including toucans, mot-mots, and resplendent quetzals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayak or paddleboard on Lake Arenal – one of Costa Rica's largest lakes with stunning volcano views. Rent equipment from a local outfitter (~$20–30) or join a guided kayak tour. Alternatively, explore the Arenal Hanging Bridges – a self-guided walk through the rainforest canopy on suspended bridges offering incredible wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Arenal Volcano Night Wildlife Walk – a guided nocturnal hike around the base of the iconic Arenal Volcano. Discover Costa Rica's hidden nightlife: red-eyed tree frogs, tarantulas, kinkajous, Jesus Christ lizards, and sleeping birds. A truly unforgettable experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your La Fortuna lodge – gallo pinto, eggs, fresh tropical fruit, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch by Lake Arenal or at a lakeside café – sandwiches, empanadas, and fresh juice (~$8–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Nene's or similar in La Fortuna before the night walk – hearty casado or grilled tilapia (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Arenal Volcano Night Wildlife Walk typically departs around 5:30–6:00 PM. Wear long sleeves, long pants, and closed-toe shoes. Bring a headlamp and insect repellent. The night walk lasts approximately 2 hours. Book in advance through a certified local operator.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart La Fortuna toward Monteverde (approximately 3–4 hours via the scenic Lake Arenal boat + jeep transfer, which is the most popular and beautiful route). Enjoy stunning lake views and rolling green hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde and check into a mid-range eco-lodge. After settling in, visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden or the Orchid Garden for a gentle, fascinating introduction to Monteverde's incredible biodiversity. These compact attractions are perfect for an afternoon exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Santa Elena village. Browse local artisan shops, pick up handcrafted souvenirs, and enjoy a relaxed dinner at one of the town's popular restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your La Fortuna lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a soda en route during the boat transfer – enjoy the lake crossing with snacks (~$5–10)
meals.dinner: Sofía Restaurant or Tree House Restaurant in Santa Elena – creative Costa Rican fusion cuisine, plantain soup, and local craft beer (~$18–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer from La Fortuna to Monteverde is a classic Costa Rica experience (~$25–35 per person) and far more scenic than the long road route. Book this transfer in advance. Roads into Monteverde are unpaved and bumpy – this is normal.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of the trip: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Multiple cables, including Superman-style lines and Tarzan swings, offer breathtaking views above the treetops. This is an iconic Costa Rican adventure experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a self-guided or guided walk through one of the world's most pristine cloud forests. Walk the well-maintained trails through moss-draped trees, listen for the three-wattled bellbird, and search for the elusive resplendent quetzal.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Bat Jungle or Frog Pond night tour in Santa Elena – a fascinating guided experience observing dozens of frog species and bat behaviors in a controlled but naturalistic setting. Perfect for wildlife enthusiasts.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your eco-lodge – fuel up before the zip-line tour with eggs, gallo pinto, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at the zip-line operator's on-site café or a nearby soda – casado plate or sandwich (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Morpho's Restaurant in Santa Elena – popular local spot with great vegetarian options, fresh pasta, and tropical desserts (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour at least 2–3 days in advance. Weight/health restrictions may apply. Wear comfortable, secure clothing and closed-toe shoes. The cloud forest reserve entrance fee is approximately $25 USD. Morning visits offer the best wildlife sightings and misty atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Guided birdwatching tour in the Monteverde area at dawn – hire a local birding guide for a 3-hour early morning walk to spot quetzals, toucans, hummingbirds, and cloud forest specialties. Monteverde is considered one of the top birding destinations in the Americas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Curi-Cancha Reserve – a quieter, less-visited cloud forest reserve adjacent to Monteverde with excellent wildlife viewing opportunities. Walk the trails at a relaxed pace, looking for sloths, coatis, and exotic birds. Alternatively, visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory (La Lechería) for a tour and tasting – a unique cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Travel day preparation: Pack bags and arrange your transfer toward the Caribbean coast for Tortuguero (typically requires traveling to San José first). Enjoy a final Monteverde dinner and get an early night.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at the lodge before the birdwatching tour – light meal with coffee and fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Curi-Cancha Reserve's café or a nearby soda – fresh salad, soup, and juice (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: El Jardín Restaurant at your lodge or a nearby mid-range option – grilled chicken in chimichurri, rice, and local vegetables (~$18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a birding guide through your lodge or a reputable local operator – early morning (5:30–6:00 AM departure) is essential for quetzal sightings. Curi-Cancha Reserve entrance is approximately $15 USD and far less crowded than the main reserve.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Monteverde early and travel to San José (approximately 3–4 hours by shuttle). From San José, take a pre-arranged transfer or public bus to Cariari, then a boat through the jungle canals to reach Tortuguero (approximately 2–3 hours total from Cariari).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tortuguero village – a car-free, canal-laced community accessible only by boat or plane. Check into a mid-range eco-lodge on the canal. Take a short orientation walk through the village and visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about Tortuguero's famous sea turtle nesting programs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your first Tortuguero canal sunset from the lodge dock. Dine at the lodge or a local restaurant in the village and listen to the sounds of the surrounding jungle as night falls.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Monteverde lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in San José during the transit layover – visit the Central Market for a traditional casado at a market soda (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Tortuguero eco-lodge restaurant or Miss Junie's – a beloved local institution serving Caribbean-style rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, jerk chicken, and fresh plantains (~$15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The journey to Tortuguero is long but scenic and part of the adventure. Book the full transfer (shuttle + boat) as a package through operators like Viajes Caribe or your lodge. Tortuguero has no ATMs – bring sufficient cash. February is a good time to visit as it's the dry season on the Caribbean side.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari. Glide through jungle canals in a small boat guided by a certified naturalist to observe manatees, caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, howler monkeys, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including kingfishers, herons, and anhingas. This is wildlife viewing at its finest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tortuguero National Park on foot via the park's jungle trail – one of the few hiking opportunities in this otherwise water-based park. The trail winds through primary rainforest and offers excellent wildlife encounters. Alternatively, rent a kayak and paddle the smaller canals independently for a more intimate experience.
day_by_day.evening: If timing aligns (February is not peak nesting season, but leatherback sea turtles begin arriving), join a certified guided sea turtle beach walk with a licensed guide. If turtles are not nesting, enjoy a night canal boat tour to spot caimans, nocturnal birds, and sleeping iguanas by spotlight.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your eco-lodge before the morning boat safari – gallo pinto, eggs, Caribbean-style bread, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch back at the lodge or a local village soda – rice and beans Caribbean style, fried fish, and fresh coconut water (~$8–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your lodge or a local restaurant – Caribbean lobster or shrimp in coconut sauce with rice and fried plantains (~$20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Wildlife Boat Safari should be booked with your lodge in advance. Smaller boats (6 passengers maximum) provide better wildlife viewing. Bring binoculars, a camera with zoom, and rain gear. The park entrance fee is approximately $15 USD. Sea turtle watching (if available) requires a licensed guide and is strictly regulated.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Tortuguero by boat and shuttle, returning toward San José. From San José, continue south toward the Osa Peninsula for the Corcovado National Park experience. This is a longer travel day – depart early. Alternatively, take a domestic flight from San José to Puerto Jiménez (highly recommended to save time, ~$90–120 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Puerto Jiménez – the gateway town to the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado National Park. Check into a mid-range eco-lodge. Explore the charming small town, visit the waterfront, and spot scarlet macaws – they are incredibly common here and a spectacular sight.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a pre-trip briefing for the Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition the following day. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Puerto Jiménez and get an early night to prepare for an adventurous day ahead.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Tortuguero lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in San José airport or food court during transit – sandwiches and fresh juice (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Carolina or Jagua Restaurant in Puerto Jiménez – fresh grilled mahi-mahi, rice and beans, and a cold local beer (~$16–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A domestic flight from San José to Puerto Jiménez with SANSA Airlines is highly recommended to avoid a 6–8 hour road journey. Book well in advance. The Osa Peninsula is remote – cash is essential as card facilities are limited. Confirm your Corcovado expedition booking and obtain your park permit in advance (required).

day_by_day.morning: The crown jewel of the trip: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition. Venture deep into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through primary rainforest with an expert naturalist guide, searching for tapirs, peccaries, jaguars (tracks), four species of monkeys, harpy eagles, and the elusive baird's tapir. Cross rivers and explore pristine jungle far from any crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the jungle expedition deeper into the park. Visit a remote beach within Corcovado, swim in a jungle river pool, and enjoy a packed lunch surrounded by untouched wilderness. The afternoon offers continued wildlife tracking and forest exploration with your expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Jiménez by late afternoon. Rest, shower, and reflect on an extraordinary day in one of the world's great wilderness areas. Enjoy a celebratory dinner with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at your lodge before 5:30 AM departure – energy-rich meal with eggs, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed jungle lunch provided by your tour operator or lodge – sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Il Giardino or a top mid-range restaurant in Puerto Jiménez – pasta, grilled catch of the day, tropical dessert, and local craft beer (~$22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires a mandatory licensed guide – independent entry is not permitted. Book your expedition through a certified operator (Osa Wild, Corcovado Expeditions, etc.) well in advance. Park entrance fee is approximately $15–20 USD. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots, long clothing, and bring plenty of water and insect repellent. This is a full, physically demanding day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Osa Peninsula: Take a gentle sunrise walk through Puerto Jiménez to spot scarlet macaws, parrots, and coastal birds. Visit a local bakery for a final Costa Rican coffee and freshly baked pan dulce. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Puerto Jiménez by domestic flight or ground transfer back to San José. If time allows before your international flight, visit the Jade Museum or Gold Museum in downtown San José for a fascinating glimpse into Costa Rica's pre-Columbian history. Do last-minute souvenir shopping at the Central Market.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Juan Santamaría International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of cloud forests, volcanoes, jungle canals, zip-lines, and wildlife encounters across one of the most biodiverse countries on the planet. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at your Puerto Jiménez lodge or a local café – gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, and the best Costa Rican coffee you've had all trip
meals.lunch: Lunch in San José – visit Kalu Café or Sikwa Restaurant for a memorable final meal showcasing Costa Rican ingredients (~$18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or aboard your flight home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your domestic flight timing carefully and arrive at the Puerto Jiménez airstrip at least 45 minutes early. SANSA flights are small and punctual. Allow at least 3 hours at San José's international airport for check-in and security. Purchase final souvenirs (coffee, chocolate, hot sauce) at the airport duty-free if you missed them in town. No biological materials, plants, or wildlife products may be exported.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges. Spot howler monkeys, toucans, and resplendent quetzals while gliding above the treetops at speeds up to 50 mph.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through jungle canals in a small boat guided by a certified naturalist to observe manatees, caimans, river otters, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the black-sand beaches at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a professional naturalist guide who uses high-powered telescopes to reveal sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, squirrel monkeys, and scarlet macaws hidden in the lush rainforest. The hike concludes at pristine white-sand beaches perfect for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Night Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided nocturnal hike around the base of the iconic Arenal Volcano to discover Costa Rica's hidden nightlife — red-eyed tree frogs, tarantulas, kinkajous, and sleeping birds. Expert guides illuminate the dark jungle trails and share fascinating insights into the rainforest ecosystem after dark.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition
experiences.description: Venture deep into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through old-growth primary rainforest with a licensed guide to encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, harpy eagles, and all four of Costa Rica's monkey species in their untouched natural habitat.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer with a bilingual chauffeur will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a chilled welcome drink and light turndown snack prepared by the resort upon check-in. Review your itinerary with the dedicated concierge and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: On board or at the airport
meals.lunch: On board or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity at the resort – charcuterie board, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine arranged in-room by the butler service

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged. Request early check-in preparation so the suite is fully ready upon late arrival. Keep Day 2 morning relaxed to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely sleep-in and late breakfast at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront property, meet your dedicated concierge, and review the full 13-day experience schedule. Enjoy a complimentary resort welcome spa treatment (30-minute aromatherapy massage) to reset after travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort snorkeling or kayaking excursion along the coastline arranged through the hotel's water sports center. Alternatively, lounge at the infinity pool with curated tropical cocktails and unwind before the adventure-packed days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the private beach terrace, followed by a multi-course chef's tasting dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant featuring locally sourced Costa Rican ingredients and farm-to-table cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant – fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict with plantain, freshly squeezed guanábana juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – ceviche, grilled fish tacos, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant – 6-course dinner with wine pairing, featuring local sea bass, hearts of palm salad, and guaro-infused desserts

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate recovery and orientation day. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings with the concierge today, including guide assignments, transport logistics, and any dietary requirements.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided Manuel Antonio National Park Eco-Hike beginning at 6:00 AM to catch peak wildlife activity. Your certified naturalist guide uses high-powered spotting scopes and binoculars to locate sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs in their natural habitat. The park is only a short drive from the resort's coastal area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Manuel Antonio's pristine white-sand beaches within the park boundaries. Swim in the crystal-clear waters of Playa Manuel Antonio, a protected cove inside the park. Return to the resort by mid-afternoon for a refreshing dip in the infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a cliffside bar overlooking the Pacific, followed by dinner at a premium local restaurant in Quepos specializing in fresh-caught seafood and traditional Costa Rican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike early breakfast at the resort – protein-rich spread with eggs, granola, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed on the beach inside Manuel Antonio Park
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Cantina de Manuel Antonio or equivalent premium Quepos restaurant – whole grilled red snapper, patacones, and local craft beer or fine wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Manuel Antonio Park gates early (opens at 7:00 AM, but private guided access can begin at 6:00 AM). Wear neutral-colored, moisture-wicking clothing and biodegradable sunscreen. Bring binoculars. Park entry fees are included in the guided experience package.

day_by_day.morning: Depart resort early by private luxury vehicle for the scenic 3.5-hour transfer to the Osa Peninsula / Corcovado region. En route, stop at a premium coffee estate in the highlands for a private single-origin coffee tasting and plantation tour with the estate owner.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at a luxury eco-lodge near Corcovado and check in. Begin your Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition with a certified naturalist guide – trek through primary rainforest, cross jungle rivers, and encounter tapirs, peccaries, poison dart frogs, and an extraordinary array of bird species including the rare harpy eagle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a nature debriefing session with your guide over cocktails. Enjoy a farm-to-jungle dinner prepared with ingredients sourced entirely from the surrounding ecosystem and local indigenous communities.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet jungle lunch prepared by the expedition team mid-trek – fresh tropical fruits, artisan sandwiches, and natural coconut water
meals.dinner: Private dinner at the Corcovado eco-lodge – rainforest-inspired tasting menu with locally hunted-and-gathered ingredients, paired with Costa Rican craft spirits

day_by_day.notes: This is an overnight excursion away from Aegean Bliss Resort. Pack a dedicated overnight bag with jungle-appropriate gear: waterproof boots, insect repellent, rain poncho, and a headlamp. The eco-lodge should be pre-booked at a premium level (e.g., Lapa Rios Lodge or equivalent).

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn guided wildlife walk inside Corcovado National Park at 5:00 AM – the most magical time to observe scarlet macaws, tapirs at watering holes, and spider monkeys in the canopy. Your naturalist guide provides expert commentary on the park's extraordinary biodiversity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic boat transfer along the Osa Peninsula coastline back toward the mainland, with opportunities to spot dolphins, sea turtles, and humpback whales (February is prime season). Private luxury transfer returns you to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome-back relaxation at the resort. Enjoy a private couples' or solo sunset yoga session on the beach arranged by the resort's wellness team, followed by a relaxing hydrotherapy session at the spa.

meals.breakfast: Early jungle breakfast at the eco-lodge before the pre-dawn walk – energy bars, tropical fruits, and hot coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant in Puerto Jiménez during the return journey
meals.dinner: Back at Aegean Bliss Resort – light, restorative dinner at the spa restaurant featuring organic salads, grilled vegetables, and fresh catch of the day

day_by_day.notes: The boat transfer from Osa back to the mainland is a highlight in itself – inform the captain you are interested in marine wildlife spotting. February is peak humpback whale season on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort spa morning – enjoy a 90-minute volcanic stone massage followed by a private yoga class on the beachfront pavilion. This is a deliberate rest day after the Corcovado expedition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private surf lesson arranged through the resort with a certified instructor on a nearby beginner-friendly beach break. Alternatively, take a private stand-up paddleboard tour along the coastline with a guide.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside bonfire dinner arranged exclusively for you by the resort's events team – a personal chef grills fresh lobster, jumbo shrimp, and local fish over open flame while a guitarist plays traditional Costa Rican music under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet in-room breakfast delivered by butler service – freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit platter, smoked salmon, and freshly brewed Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Beachfront ceviche bar at the resort – three types of fresh ceviche, plantain chips, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Private beachside bonfire dinner – grilled lobster, jumbo shrimp, whole fish, and tropical desserts with champagne

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally luxurious and low-key, providing physical recovery between the Corcovado expedition and the upcoming multi-day journey to Tortuguero and Monteverde. Confirm all upcoming transfers and bookings with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Aegean Bliss Resort by private luxury vehicle for the journey toward the Caribbean coast. En route, stop at a premium chocolate plantation in the Turrialba region for a private bean-to-bar chocolate-making experience with the master chocolatier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the gateway town of La Pavona and board a private motorized canoe through the jungle waterways toward Tortuguero Village. Check in to a premium eco-lodge within or adjacent to Tortuguero National Park (e.g., Tortuga Lodge or equivalent).
day_by_day.evening: Introductory guided walk along Tortuguero beach at dusk to orient yourself to the environment. Enjoy a welcome cocktail reception at the lodge, followed by a candlelit dinner with views of the jungle canals.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Premium lunch stop at a hacienda restaurant in the Central Valley highlands – traditional casado with locally raised beef and farm-fresh vegetables
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Tortuguero eco-lodge – Caribbean-inspired cuisine featuring rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, fresh river fish, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: This is a second overnight excursion. Pack a second overnight bag. Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small aircraft – no roads reach the village. The private canoe transfer is an experience in itself. Bring waterproof bags for all electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari at 6:00 AM – glide silently through the network of jungle canals in a small private boat with a certified naturalist guide. Observe river otters, manatees, caimans, green iguanas, Jesus Christ lizards, toucans, kingfishers, and multiple monkey species. The early morning light creates extraordinary photography opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for lunch, then embark on a private kayaking tour through narrower jungle waterways inaccessible to motorized boats – a more intimate and silent wildlife encounter. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about Tortuguero's legendary nesting sea turtle populations.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat tour on the main Tortuguero canal, followed by a cultural evening at the lodge featuring a traditional Caribbean cooking class with the head chef, learning to prepare authentic Caribbean rice and beans, patacones, and plantain desserts.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast at the lodge before the boat safari – fresh fruit, granola, and coffee
meals.lunch: Full Caribbean lunch at the lodge – coconut shrimp, fried plantains, and fresh tropical juice
meals.dinner: Caribbean cooking class dinner – dishes you prepare yourself with the chef, paired with local Guaro cocktails and Caribbean rum

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is one of the most important sea turtle nesting sites in the world. While February is not peak nesting season (July–October), the wildlife boat safari remains world-class year-round. Wear dark, muted clothing for early morning wildlife observation. Silence is essential on the canals.

day_by_day.morning: Final early morning birdwatching walk through Tortuguero village with your guide, spotting species unique to the Caribbean lowlands. Depart Tortuguero by private boat and luxury transfer, beginning the scenic journey toward the Monteverde Cloud Forest region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Monteverde/Santa Elena area after a 4–5 hour transfer through the Central Valley. Check in to a premium cloud forest lodge (e.g., Monteverde Lodge & Gardens or equivalent). Take a private orientation walk through the lodge's private forest reserve to begin acclimatizing to the cloud forest ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge's viewing deck overlooking the Nicoya Gulf and the Pacific lowlands far below. Enjoy a refined dinner at the lodge's restaurant, one of the finest in the Monteverde region.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Tortuguero eco-lodge – full Caribbean spread
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch stop at a premium restaurant in Ciudad Quesada (San Carlos) during the transfer – traditional Costa Rican cuisine with a contemporary twist
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Monteverde cloud forest lodge restaurant – highland-inspired menu featuring local cheese fondue, cloud forest mushroom risotto, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde is famously rough in sections – even in a luxury 4WD vehicle, expect some bumpy stretches. The journey is scenic and worth it. Bring a light jacket as Monteverde is significantly cooler than the coast (15–22°C / 59–72°F).

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – the crown jewel of Costa Rican zip-lining. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable circuit featuring Costa Rica's longest and fastest zip-lines. Your private guide provides ecological commentary between platforms, highlighting the unique cloud forest ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve with a private naturalist guide for a 3-hour guided hike. Spot the legendary resplendent quetzal (February is excellent season as males display their brilliant plumage), three-wattled bellbirds, and the extraordinary diversity of orchids and bromeliads.
day_by_day.evening: Arenal Volcano Night Wildlife Walk – transfer to the Arenal region (approximately 2 hours from Monteverde) and join a guided nocturnal hike around the base of the iconic Arenal Volcano. Discover red-eyed tree frogs, fer-de-lance snakes, kinkajous, and a symphony of nocturnal insects and amphibians.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the cloud forest lodge – highland eggs, local cheese, and freshly brewed Monteverde coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium café in Santa Elena – cloud forest mushroom soup, artisan sandwiches, and local cheese platters
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant near Arenal – grilled meats and local vegetables with views of the illuminated volcano

day_by_day.notes: This is an exceptionally full day combining two of the most iconic Costa Rican experiences. The zip-line tour should be booked for early morning (8:00 AM) to catch the mist. The night walk begins at 7:00 PM. Wear layers – temperatures vary significantly between Monteverde and Arenal.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal – one of the most scenic lakes in Central America with the perfect cone of Arenal Volcano as a backdrop. Your guide identifies bird species along the lakeshore, including ospreys, herons, and kingfishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to La Fortuna's famous Tabacón Hot Springs – soak in the natural thermal waters fed by Arenal Volcano's geothermal energy. This premium resort's hot springs are among the finest in the world, featuring multiple pools at varying temperatures surrounded by tropical gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey toward the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a private transfer with a stop for dinner at a premium restaurant in the Central Valley, arriving back at the resort late evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal area lodge – full tropical spread with volcano views
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort's restaurant – gourmet Costa Rican cuisine enjoyed poolside in the thermal gardens
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Alajuela or San José during the return transfer – contemporary Costa Rican fusion cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tabacón Hot Springs for the premium 'Gran Spa' package which includes exclusive pool access, towels, and a food and beverage credit. The return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort will take approximately 3–4 hours from La Fortuna – plan for a late arrival (10:00–11:00 PM).

day_by_day.morning: Final full day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Begin with a private sunrise yoga session on the beach, followed by a comprehensive 2-hour spa journey – couples' or solo treatment featuring a volcanic mud wrap, exfoliation, and a signature deep-tissue massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chartered boat tour along the coastline for a final wildlife and marine encounter – spot spinner dolphins, sea turtles, and magnificent frigatebirds. Anchor in a secluded cove for snorkeling over pristine coral reefs with a marine biologist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue – a specially arranged private chef's table experience on the beachfront terrace. The resort's executive chef prepares a bespoke 8-course tasting menu celebrating the finest ingredients of Costa Rica, paired with premium wines selected by the resort's sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious champagne breakfast in bed delivered by butler service – smoked salmon, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch served on the charter boat in the secluded cove – lobster rolls, chilled shrimp, artisan cheeses, and chilled Chablis
meals.dinner: Private chef's table farewell dinner on the beachfront – 8-course tasting menu with premium wine pairing, ending with a personalized dessert and Costa Rican chocolate experience

day_by_day.notes: This is the final full day – make it count. Request the resort's photography team to document the farewell dinner for a premium keepsake photo package. Begin packing this evening and confirm departure logistics with the concierge for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxed last breakfast at the oceanfront restaurant, take a final walk along the beach, and check out at the agreed time. Private luxury transfer departs for Juan Santamaría International Airport with ample time for international departure procedures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport arrival and check-in. Access the premium international lounge for final refreshments, Costa Rican coffee, and last-minute souvenir shopping at the airport's artisan boutiques featuring locally made crafts, coffee, and chocolate.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, and luxury experiences in one of the world's most biodiverse destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – a full spread of your favorites from the past 13 days
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge lunch or in-flight premium dining
meals.dinner: In-flight premium dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international check-in and security at Juan Santamaría Airport. The private transfer should be scheduled to depart the resort approximately 4–4.5 hours before your flight. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES international wildlife trade regulations – avoid purchasing any products made from wildlife. Declare all food items at customs.

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
